📅 FULL CARD RECAP — 8/29/2026 · Saratoga
Dirt speed carried far and died late — press/stalk horses won 7 of 9 dirt races; only Englishman wired, and every other front-ender got run down inside the 1/16. Firm turf: nobody wanted the lead — crawling halves (48.8–49.7) in three routes; commitment beat figures on grass all day. Stakes chalk stood up but the Travers went 10/1 and the finale 17/1. Prat won FIVE (four for Chad Brown); fresh horses off 2–10 month benches won four — layoff barns were live.
🏁 RACE RECAP — 8/29/2026 RACE 12 · Saratoga
The two need-the-lead mares (Maida 23/1, R Disaster 6/1) hooked up in 44.1 and both died — textbook melt; Ways and Means (7/5) sat just off it and ran off. Both speed mares forgiven vs a softer front. Kilwin closed for 2nd — needs pace, under horse. Beauty Reigns big late move for 3rd AGAIN — keeps knocking at 12/1, wins one of these when the front goes fast.

📅 FULL CARD RECAP — 8/29/2026 · Saratoga
Dirt speed carried far and died late — press/stalk horses won 7 of 9 dirt races; only Englishman wired, and every other front-ender got run down inside the 1/16. Firm turf: nobody wanted the lead — crawling halves (48.8–49.7) in three routes; commitment beat figures on grass all day. Stakes chalk stood up but the Travers went 10/1 and the finale 17/1. Prat won FIVE (four for Chad Brown); fresh horses off 2–10 month benches won four — layoff barns were live.
🏁 RACE RECAP — 8/29/2026 RACE 12 · Saratoga
The two need-the-lead mares (Maida 23/1, R Disaster 6/1) hooked up in 44.1 and both died — textbook melt; Ways and Means (7/5) sat just off it and ran off. Both speed mares forgiven vs a softer front. Kilwin closed for 2nd — needs pace, under horse. Beauty Reigns big late move for 3rd AGAIN — keeps knocking at 12/1, wins one of these when the front goes fast.

🎤 QUOTE — 8/26/2026
TDZONE after Nunthorpe -- On a softer surface at York on Friday afternoon, Bacio was sensational as he flew to the front with an opening furlong of 13.0s and from that moment on, he didn’t ever look like he was going to be headed. Horses don’t really win Group 1 sprints like that and Bacio’s average stride frequency figures of 2.57 strides per second was 6.6% higher than the expected average for a winner of this race. To put that into more basic terms, that means that Bacio was taking around 1.5 strides per furlong more than an average winner. He needed to do that because his average stride length of 22.76 ft was the shortest of the 18 runners in the field, but the ability to move his feet that quickly on a much softer surface than he encountered at Ascot, meant that he had most of this field in trouble at halfway. -- Once shaken up, his mount found enough to get to the line and for all of Bacio’s perceived speed, it is worth noting that the only time he ran the fastest split in the field was for the first furlong and his top speed figure of 41.97 mph ranked only 12th. He has won 2 races in very impressive fashion, but he might actually be better around a bend and if he does go to the Breeders’ Cup and gets a reasonably low draw, he is probably going to prove to be unbeatable!!

The ten-furlong went to the mare who sat sixth and came five wide after a sent pretender made it honest and the presser folded.
🏁 RACE RECAP — 10/1/2026 RACE 6 · Belmont
* Our single went four wide again and ran third at 2/1 while our 2nd choice wired from the rail * T Kraft (6/1) tough hard hitter in good form * Senior Officer (2/1) solid at this level * Crazy Mason (5/1) prefer underneath at this level * Fade Moonlight (7/2) at a short price in the East until he shows his California number here
📅 FULL CARD RECAP — 8/29/2026 · Saratoga
Dirt speed carried far and died late — press/stalk horses won 7 of 9 dirt races; only Englishman wired, and every other front-ender got run down inside the 1/16. Firm turf: nobody wanted the lead — crawling halves (48.8–49.7) in three routes; commitment beat figures on grass all day. Stakes chalk stood up but the Travers went 10/1 and the finale 17/1. Prat won FIVE (four for Chad Brown); fresh horses off 2–10 month benches won four — layoff barns were live.
🏁 RACE RECAP — 8/29/2026 RACE 11 · Saratoga
Tip Top Thomas (9/5) first try at 7f, led to the 3/16, weakened — not disgraced; back at 6-6.5f he wins. Hymn (9/2) pressed and outfought them. T Kraft dead-heated 2nd at 23/1 off a career-best — he’s for real now, don’t let that price happen again. Crazy Mason, 62 days off, missed by under a length for ALL of it at 8/1 — wins next at this trip. Bring the Smoke broke bad AGAIN (that’s 5 of 7) — toss until he proves he can break.

1 Gimme A Nother
H Graham Motion · J R Velazquez · 10-1
📅 FULL CARD RECAP — 9/12/2026 · Woodbine
Two surfaces, one afternoon The Tapeta held speed — four of five won on the lead, and not off soft fractions: the two synthetic stakes ran 44.68 and 46.83 to the half, both nearly two seconds under par, and the leaders still had plenty. Both turf courses were the exact inverse: six of seven winners came from off the pace, and every one came wide — seven-path, five-wide, five-wide, five-wide, a three-path seam, three-wide. Path, blunt: on turf, get off the fence. Rail trips produced nothing but tired horses all day even with the inner rail out 32 feet, while four-plus-wide closers were rewarded rather than taxed. On the Tapeta path barely mattered and position did — three of the four synthetic winners crossed to the rail and sat there. The sharpest line on the card is in the stakes: four of five graded races won from off the pace, the fifth from an uncontested lead, and every graded front-runner who was actually engaged lost. RACE BY RACE

2 Evershed
Arnaud Delacour · Mickael Barzalona · 30-1
📅 FULL CARD RECAP — 10/1/2026 · Belmont
8 races, all dry: Dirt 4 (R1 R2 R3 R6) · Widener turf 2 (R4 R7) · Inner turf 2 (R5 R8) Dirt (4 races: R1 R2 R3 R6): THE SPEED HELD WHEN IT WAS THE BEST HORSE — three of four fronts won ; the one that folded went quick early with a cheap presser at its side and the race came to the stalker sitting Widener turf (2 races: R4 R7): CHEAP SPEED FOLDED, CLOSERS CAME OFF — the mile's rail leader went slow in front and still stopped, the two who finished first and third came from fourth and seventh, and the twelve-furlong crawl went to the horse sitting fourth behind cover; the Widener's mile races so far have played well to off pace runners Inner turf (2 races: R5 R8): the 6F front the first and third home skimmed the rail from behind the pace. The ten-furlong went to the mare who sat sixth and came five wide after a sent pretender made it honest and the presser folded.
🏁 RACE RECAP — 10/1/2026 RACE 8 · Belmont
* Kathynmarissa, our top pick, ran her number for the fifth straight time — five wide from sixth over an honest pace, by three-quarters at 7/5 — while our second pick Cathedral pressed from post 10 and folded to eighth * Kathynmarissa (7/5) wins again at 9–10 furlongs * Sunlit Uplands (6/1) answered the trip and is live at a price * Evershed (32/1) is live at a price * Fade Gezora (6/1) at a short price until a top figure returns
📅 FULL CARD RECAP — 8/28/2026 · Saratoga
No wire jobs all day. All 5 dirt winners rallied from just off it, finishing 3-9 wide — plain dirt speed lost all day. Both turf routes won by the pocket trip behind the speed. Prat won 4. Kantarmaci barns hot at prices (won R2, 2nds R3+R4).
🏁 RACE RECAP — 8/28/2026 RACE 8 · Saratoga
Crawl (50.7 half). Leader got a dream trip, still picked off by the horse on her hip at the hedge. Nothing closed from the back — slow turf routes here: be the pocket. Massarat rank in the crawl, still closed — wants tempo. Snipsnippitysnip steadied at the 3/8 — better than line will suggest.

She put on a good race on top of that, had some kind of a bad trip, had to make a wide middle move that I don’t really like with those kind of horses — usually I like to be more patient and make one run — but it served its purpose, she got something out of it and moved up even better.

8 Jancis
Willie Mccreery · Billy Lee · 20-1
📅 FULL CARD RECAP — 9/12/2026 · Woodbine
Two surfaces, one afternoon The Tapeta held speed — four of five won on the lead, and not off soft fractions: the two synthetic stakes ran 44.68 and 46.83 to the half, both nearly two seconds under par, and the leaders still had plenty. Both turf courses were the exact inverse: six of seven winners came from off the pace, and every one came wide — seven-path, five-wide, five-wide, five-wide, a three-path seam, three-wide. Path, blunt: on turf, get off the fence. Rail trips produced nothing but tired horses all day even with the inner rail out 32 feet, while four-plus-wide closers were rewarded rather than taxed. On the Tapeta path barely mattered and position did — three of the four synthetic winners crossed to the rail and sat there. The sharpest line on the card is in the stakes: four of five graded races won from off the pace, the fifth from an uncontested lead, and every graded front-runner who was actually engaged lost. RACE BY RACE

1 Mad House

📅 FULL CARD RECAP — 10/2/2026 · Keeneland
10 races, showery, the turf good after a noon rain: Dirt 7 (R1 R2 R3 R4 R6 R7 R9) · Turf 3 (R5 R8 R10) Dirt (7 races: R1 R2 R3 R4 R6 R7 R9): the pressed fronts folded in all four sprints and the horse sitting just off them, or the one closing from last, won every time; the three leaders nobody pressed hard > wired. The main track was quick for the level all day Turf (3 races: R5 R8 R10): Rail at 20 ft. THE INSIDE PATH WON ALL THREE — the inside stalker, the rail stalker and the inside presser; the wide movers never landed and the fronts went 0-for-3. The going was slow after the rain and every turf time came back well over par: throw the turf clockings
🏁 RACE RECAP — 10/2/2026 RACE 7 · Keeneland
* Two speeds went at it hard and the one-run closer got them * Nakatomi (5/2), the seven-year-old defending winner, came from last up the inside and drove past late — the closer a hot pace set up * Little Thunder (8/1) stalked wide and ran 2nd — the seat is his, the class the question; underneath may need softer * Mad House (5/1) pressed every yard and held 3rd — live with an easier lead * Verifire (8/5), the favorite with the year's best figure, faded to 7th — a bounce or a trip watching next

📅 FULL CARD RECAP — 8/29/2026 · Saratoga
Dirt speed carried far and died late — press/stalk horses won 7 of 9 dirt races; only Englishman wired, and every other front-ender got run down inside the 1/16. Firm turf: nobody wanted the lead — crawling halves (48.8–49.7) in three routes; commitment beat figures on grass all day. Stakes chalk stood up but the Travers went 10/1 and the finale 17/1. Prat won FIVE (four for Chad Brown); fresh horses off 2–10 month benches won four — layoff barns were live.
🏁 RACE RECAP — 8/29/2026 RACE 11 · Saratoga
Tip Top Thomas (9/5) first try at 7f, led to the 3/16, weakened — not disgraced; back at 6-6.5f he wins. Hymn (9/2) pressed and outfought them. T Kraft dead-heated 2nd at 23/1 off a career-best — he’s for real now, don’t let that price happen again. Crazy Mason, 62 days off, missed by under a length for ALL of it at 8/1 — wins next at this trip. Bring the Smoke broke bad AGAIN (that’s 5 of 7) — toss until he proves he can break.

📅 FULL CARD RECAP — 10/2/2026 · Keeneland
10 races, showery, the turf good after a noon rain: Dirt 7 (R1 R2 R3 R4 R6 R7 R9) · Turf 3 (R5 R8 R10) Dirt (7 races: R1 R2 R3 R4 R6 R7 R9): the pressed fronts folded in all four sprints and the horse sitting just off them, or the one closing from last, won every time; the three leaders nobody pressed hard > wired. The main track was quick for the level all day Turf (3 races: R5 R8 R10): Rail at 20 ft. THE INSIDE PATH WON ALL THREE — the inside stalker, the rail stalker and the inside presser; the wide movers never landed and the fronts went 0-for-3. The going was slow after the rain and every turf time came back well over par: throw the turf clockings

FanDuel Breeders' Cup Mile
RACE 9 · 4:20 PM ET · $2,000,000 Grade 1 · 1 Mile Turf
1 Deterministic
Miguel Clement · K Carmouche · 8-1
📅 FULL CARD RECAP — 9/12/2026 · Woodbine
Two surfaces, one afternoon The Tapeta held speed — four of five won on the lead, and not off soft fractions: the two synthetic stakes ran 44.68 and 46.83 to the half, both nearly two seconds under par, and the leaders still had plenty. Both turf courses were the exact inverse: six of seven winners came from off the pace, and every one came wide — seven-path, five-wide, five-wide, five-wide, a three-path seam, three-wide. Path, blunt: on turf, get off the fence. Rail trips produced nothing but tired horses all day even with the inner rail out 32 feet, while four-plus-wide closers were rewarded rather than taxed. On the Tapeta path barely mattered and position did — three of the four synthetic winners crossed to the rail and sat there. The sharpest line on the card is in the stakes: four of five graded races won from off the pace, the fifth from an uncontested lead, and every graded front-runner who was actually engaged lost. RACE BY RACE
🏁 RACE RECAP — 9/12/2026 RACE 9 · Woodbine
WOODBINE MILE (G1) · 3yo+ · 1M turf * Deterministic got the trip of the race — a moderate 47.89, alone, in the clear — and was still run down inside the sixteenth; he is a very good horse who couldn’t quite hold off the Appleby monster > Notable Speech angled five wide from fifth and went past him. * ITSASTORMYMONDAY at 70/1 came from last SEVEN wide for fourth — an enormous price and a real run; watch for him dropping to a softer spot. * Gas Me Up (20/1) was keen early, saved ground and angled four wide for third — he keeps hitting the board at odds and belongs underneath.

📅 FULL CARD RECAP — 9/12/2026 · Woodbine
Two surfaces, one afternoon The Tapeta held speed — four of five won on the lead, and not off soft fractions: the two synthetic stakes ran 44.68 and 46.83 to the half, both nearly two seconds under par, and the leaders still had plenty. Both turf courses were the exact inverse: six of seven winners came from off the pace, and every one came wide — seven-path, five-wide, five-wide, five-wide, a three-path seam, three-wide. Path, blunt: on turf, get off the fence. Rail trips produced nothing but tired horses all day even with the inner rail out 32 feet, while four-plus-wide closers were rewarded rather than taxed. On the Tapeta path barely mattered and position did — three of the four synthetic winners crossed to the rail and sat there. The sharpest line on the card is in the stakes: four of five graded races won from off the pace, the fifth from an uncontested lead, and every graded front-runner who was actually engaged lost. RACE BY RACE
🏁 RACE RECAP — 9/12/2026 RACE 9 · Woodbine
WOODBINE MILE (G1) · 3yo+ · 1M turf * Deterministic got the trip of the race — a moderate 47.89, alone, in the clear — and was still run down inside the sixteenth; he is a very good horse who couldn’t quite hold off the Appleby monster > Notable Speech angled five wide from fifth and went past him. * ITSASTORMYMONDAY at 70/1 came from last SEVEN wide for fourth — an enormous price and a real run; watch for him dropping to a softer spot. * Gas Me Up (20/1) was keen early, saved ground and angled four wide for third — he keeps hitting the board at odds and belongs underneath.

📅 FULL CARD RECAP — 9/25/2026 · Belmont
9 races, all dry: Dirt 4 (R1 R2 R4 R7) · inner turf 2 (R5 R8) · Widener turf 3 (R3 R6 R9). Dirt (4 races: R1 R2 R4 R7): TWO WIRES BY THE BEST SPEED — a first-timer with the top gate drill led all the way in the 2yo filly sprint and the champ Nitrogen did it in hand in the Beldame; the mile's leader held 2nd through a real pace, and the only cheap front (the 7f 2yo) folded to the pocket. Five wires in fifteen dirt races now, every one quality speed: the track is fair — the horse decides, not the surface Inner Turf (2 races: R5 R8): Rail at 36 ft. BOTH FRONTS FOLDED — a cutback dirt burner to 3rd behind the controller from 2nd, and an in-hand 38/1 leader to 6th behind the favorite from last, four wide. Cheap speed died Widener Turf (3 races: R3 R6 R9): Rail at 36 ft. QUALITY ON THE LEAD HOLDS, THE REST FOLD — the 7f leader (a second-starter off four bullets) held 2nd behind the figure filly, the mile's 19/1 rail leader folded to 4th, and the 8.5f's quickest filly wired it in hand on a soft half nobody hooked her. Takeaway: the best speed body holds and the cheap one folds, on every course. A duel on paper needs two horses who WANT the lead; today two of them sat and the leaders walked

SARATOGA SPRINGS, N.Y. – Sovereignty (Into Mischief) stayed put at Hall of Fame trainer Bill Mott's barn Saturday morning. His scheduled workout had been scrapped, and the 4-year-old colt passed the time surveying the scene from his stall on a perfect late summer day. Besides Sovereignty, Mott nominated two other horses for the Jockey Club Gold Cup. Baeza (McKinzie), fourth in the Whitney in his last start, and Stars and Stripes (Not This Time), who defeated stablemate Parchment Party (Constitution) by a nose in the Birdstone Stakes, are eligible for the Gold Cup.

Dirt speed carried far and died late — press/stalk horses won 7 of 9 dirt races; only Englishman wired, and every other front-ender got run down inside the 1/16. Firm turf: nobody wanted the lead — crawling halves (48.8–49.7) in three routes; commitment beat figures on grass all day. Stakes chalk stood up but the Travers went 10/1 and the finale 17/1. Prat won FIVE (four for Chad Brown); fresh horses off 2–10 month benches won four — layoff barns were live.
🏁 RACE RECAP — 8/29/2026 RACE 13 · Saratoga
Napoleon Solo (8/1) walked the lead — modest fractions — and STILL got caught in the last jump by Leading Change (10/1), fresh off one start since July, second off the bench for Cox: that’s a horse going forward, Breeders’ Cup quality. Napoleon Solo wins his next two-turn stakes. Golden Tempo (9/5 fav) was 16 lengths back at the half with nothing collapsing — needed a meltdown; not a fade, needs pace. Renegade LUNGED at the start and got pinched to last — race VOID, toss the line. Sea Strike pressed and emptied at 7/2 — fade at short odds in routes > prefer 7F - 9F on ped inclination

Napoleon Solo (8/1) walked the lead — modest fractions — and STILL got caught in the last jump by Leading Change (10/1), fresh off one start since July, second off the bench for Cox: that’s a horse going forward, Breeders’ Cup quality. Napoleon Solo wins his next two-turn stakes. Golden Tempo (9/5 fav) was 16 lengths back at the half with nothing collapsing — needed a meltdown; not a fade, needs pace. 📅 FULL CARD RECAP — 9/18/2026 · Belmont
Opening Day New Belmont, both rails at 36ft. I thought the turf course played fair but on the dirt you needed to be near the pace, speed-wise, with an advantage. Dirt: YOU WANTED TO BE CLOSE, NOT ON IT — zero wire jobs in four dirt races, every winner stalked or pressed from 1–4 back, five of six true fronts up the track. Times came back near or a touch slower than the OLD Belmont pars — stale yardsticks on a new track, so no conclusion - AD Inner Turf: Rail at 36 ft. Played FAIR — pace told both stories (a crawl-and-sprint, then a stolen solo walk); no path edge either race, times close to the old pars — nothing to call. - AD Widener Turf: Rail at 36 ft. Looked QUICK — the baby sprint came back 3+ seconds faster than the OLD Belmont turf par, but that's an old-surface yardstick on a brand-new course > go easy trusting big turf figures from this card on the Widener. - AD The Amelia Green Fister in the second and Freaky in the eighth were the only horses that came from out of it. All the other horses that ran in the money in the dirt races were on the lead or right off the pace. (Taking note won’t call bias till replays and checking flows) Watch horses who could be live NTO: E Z Speaker (R7) · Garden of Grace (R9) · Mary Lois (R1) · Sea Vista (R8) · Mom's On Break (R2) · Runyon Canyon (R1) NTO if back to 9F - AD

8 Napoleon Solo
Chad Summers · J R Velazquez · 15-1
📅 FULL CARD RECAP — 8/29/2026 · Saratoga
Dirt speed carried far and died late — press/stalk horses won 7 of 9 dirt races; only Englishman wired, and every other front-ender got run down inside the 1/16. Firm turf: nobody wanted the lead — crawling halves (48.8–49.7) in three routes; commitment beat figures on grass all day. Stakes chalk stood up but the Travers went 10/1 and the finale 17/1. Prat won FIVE (four for Chad Brown); fresh horses off 2–10 month benches won four — layoff barns were live.
🏁 RACE RECAP — 8/29/2026 RACE 13 · Saratoga
Napoleon Solo (8/1) walked the lead — modest fractions — and STILL got caught in the last jump by Leading Change (10/1), fresh off one start since July, second off the bench for Cox: that’s a horse going forward, Breeders’ Cup quality. Napoleon Solo wins his next two-turn stakes. Golden Tempo (9/5 fav) was 16 lengths back at the half with nothing collapsing — needed a meltdown; not a fade, needs pace. Renegade LUNGED at the start and got pinched to last — race VOID, toss the line. Sea Strike pressed and emptied at 7/2 — fade at short odds in routes > prefer 7F - 9F on ped inclination
